options: Validate module role requirements and the user’s effective role inheritance before troubleshooting UI-level causes.
Clear browser cache first because left-nav visibility is cached independently from role entitlements.
Rebuild dictionary caches first since module rendering depends on latest dictionary update timestamp.
Run module fix scripts to republish sys_ui_module records for all role maps after each role change.
csa.explanation: Module visibility is role-driven. First validate role requirements and current effective roles (including inherited group roles).

csa.q: Which combination best represents a realistic pre-production validation gate for CSA admin changes?
options: Preview in target, resolve collisions, run focused UAT, then commit with rollback plan and release evidence.
Commit to production and validate with live users because UAT environments rarely mirror real behavior.
Skip preview when update set count is small; XML exports provide equivalent dependency assurance.
Rely exclusively on ATF and bypass UAT because automated checks cover functional and operational readiness.
csa.explanation: Best practice is preview plus conflict resolution plus UAT before commit to reduce regressions and environment drift.

csa.q: Which statement about ACL evaluation is most accurate for CSA exam expectations?
options: ACL checks are operation-specific; satisfying role conditions helps but does not universally guarantee access.
A single passing ACL grants full CRUD access on the table regardless of operation context.
Read ACL success implies write ACL success when both ACLs reference the same role requirement.
Admin role bypasses ACL behavior in every execution path including delegated and scoped contexts.
csa.explanation: ACLs are operation-specific and evaluated for access decisions; role assignment helps satisfy ACL requirements but does not replace ACL logic semantics.

csa.q: A list layout shows columns differently for two users on the same table. What is the most likely explanation?
options: User-level personalization/view preferences can produce different list columns on the same table.
Dictionary metadata is duplicated per user, so each profile stores an independent column schema.
List columns are globally fixed and cannot differ unless the instance was recently cloned.
Group role inheritance enforces unique default list columns for each group membership path.
csa.explanation: ServiceNow supports user personalization for list/form layouts and view preferences, so UI can differ per user without schema differences.

csm.q: What is the primary purpose of Customer Service Management (CSM) in ServiceNow?
options: To manage customer interactions, cases, and service experiences across multiple channels
To manage internal IT incidents only
To handle employee onboarding
To manage software licenses
csm.explanation: CSM provides a platform for managing customer-facing service operations including case management, self-service portals, and multi-channel communication.

csm.q: What is an Account in CSM?
options: A record representing a company or organization that is a customer
A user login credential
A financial billing record
A type of service catalog item
csm.explanation: In CSM, an Account (customer_account table) represents an external organization that your company provides services to.

csm.q: What table stores Cases in ServiceNow CSM?
options: sn_customerservice_case
incident
sc_request
task
csm.explanation: CSM Cases are stored in the sn_customerservice_case table, which extends the task table. This is separate from the incident table used for internal IT incidents.

csm.q: What is a Contact in CSM?
options: A person associated with a customer Account who can open and track cases
Any user in the system
A phone number record
A type of notification
csm.explanation: Contacts (customer_contact table) are individuals associated with a customer Account. They can log into the customer portal, create cases, and track their organization's cases.

csm.q: What is the difference between a Contact and a Consumer in CSM?
options: Contacts are B2B (associated with an Account/organization); Consumers are B2C (individual customers not tied to an organization)
They are the same thing
Contacts can only call in; Consumers can only use the portal
Consumers have higher priority than Contacts
csm.explanation: Contacts represent people at business accounts (B2B). Consumers represent individual customers (B2C) who interact directly without an organizational relationship.

csm.q: What is the Customer Service Portal in CSM?
options: A self-service web portal where customers can create cases, check case status, browse knowledge articles, and manage their account
An internal admin dashboard
A reporting tool for CSM metrics
A configuration page for CSM settings
csm.explanation: The Customer Service Portal (built on Service Portal) provides a branded self-service experience for external customers to submit and track cases, access knowledge, and interact with the support team.

csm.q: What is a Case Type in CSM?
options: A categorization that determines the case workflow, fields, and SLA — common types include Question, Issue, and Request
The font style used in case descriptions
The severity level of a case
The channel through which a case was created
csm.explanation: Case Types categorize cases and can drive different workflows, approval processes, field visibility, and SLA targets. Standard types include Question, Issue, and Request.

csm.q: What is Agent Workspace in CSM?
options: A modern, configurable agent interface built on UI Builder that provides a unified view of customer cases, communications, and related information
A developer IDE for writing scripts
A physical office space requirement
A mobile app for field agents
csm.explanation: Agent Workspace (Configurable Workspace) provides agents with a streamlined interface showing case details, customer history, communications, and recommended actions in a single pane.

csm.q: What is an Entitlement in CSM?
options: A record that defines what service or support level a customer is entitled to, including SLA targets and available channels
A user role permission
A type of case priority
A billing invoice
csm.explanation: Entitlements define service commitments for specific customers or products. They determine SLA targets, support hours, communication channels, and service scope based on the customer's contract.

csm.q: What channels does CSM support for customer communication?
options: Phone, Email, Portal, Chat, Social Media, Walk-in — all channels are tracked and can create/update cases
Email only
Phone and Email only
Portal only
csm.explanation: CSM is omnichannel — customers can interact via phone, email, self-service portal, live chat, social media, and walk-in. All interactions are tracked against the case for a complete communication history.

csm.q: Explain the relationship between Account, Contact, Consumer, and Case in CSM.
options: An Account is the organization; Contacts are people at that organization; Consumers are B2C individuals; Cases track service requests linked to any of these
They are all the same table with different views
Contacts and Consumers are identical
Cases can only be linked to Accounts, not individuals
csm.explanation: CSM data model: Accounts (B2B organizations) have Contacts (people at those orgs). Consumers are B2C individuals. Cases can be opened by/for any of these, with relationships tracked through the case record.

csm.q: What is Major Issue Management in CSM?
options: A process for managing widespread service issues affecting multiple customers by linking child cases to a parent case for coordinated resolution and communication
A tool for managing P1 incidents only
A separate application from CSM
A reporting dashboard for escalated cases
csm.explanation: Major Issue Management creates a parent case for a widespread issue and links affected customer cases as children. Updates and resolutions flow from parent to child cases, ensuring consistent communication.

csm.q: What is the purpose of the Product model in CSM?
options: To track products and services sold to customers, linking them to accounts for entitlement verification and asset tracking
To manage software development sprints
To track internal product roadmaps
To store marketing materials
csm.explanation: The Product model (sn_customerservice_product) tracks products/services associated with customer accounts. It enables product-specific SLAs, entitlements, and knowledge, and helps agents understand what the customer is using.

csm.q: What is the Assignment Workbench in CSM?
options: A visual tool for dispatchers to assign and reassign cases to agents based on skills, availability, and workload — showing a real-time queue view
A developer tool for assigning variables
A report builder for tracking assignments
A configuration page for assignment rules
csm.explanation: The Assignment Workbench provides supervisors/dispatchers a real-time view of agent workloads and case queues. They can drag-and-drop assign cases, see agent availability, and balance workload.

csm.q: How does CSM handle SLAs differently from standard ITSM SLAs?
options: CSM commonly binds entitlement/account context into SLA targeting, rather than treating all requests through one generic SLA policy.
CSM SLAs are always faster than ITSM SLAs because customer-facing timers bypass internal workflow pauses.
CSM does not support SLA definitions; only entitlement records determine response and resolution obligations.
CSM and ITSM SLA behavior is identical in all cases once case and incident share the same priority value.
csm.explanation: CSM SLAs integrate with Entitlements to provide customer-specific service levels. A premium customer might have a 1-hour response SLA while a standard customer has 4 hours, all managed through entitlement records linked to accounts.

csm.q: What is a Playbook in CSM and how does it guide agents?
options: Playbooks orchestrate guided agent actions with context-aware tasks/decisions to standardize complex case handling.
Playbooks are static knowledge articles that agents open when no workflow automation is available.
Playbooks replace assignment rules by deciding which group owns a case at creation time.
Playbooks should execute only after case closure to document what actions were taken by agents.
csm.explanation: Playbooks provide structured guidance through Process Automation Designer. They present agents with sequential steps, required fields, and decision points, ensuring consistent case handling across the team.

csm.q: What is the Special Handling Note feature in CSM?
options: Alerts that appear when an agent opens a case for a specific customer, displaying important information like VIP status, known issues, or special procedures
A field for internal notes on the case
A post-it note feature in the UI
A type of email template
csm.explanation: Special Handling Notes are proactive alerts tied to accounts, contacts, or consumers. When an agent works on a case for a flagged customer, the note prominently displays critical information (e.g., 'VIP Client — escalate immediately').

csm.q: What is the difference between the CSM portal and the Service Portal used for ITSM?
options: CSM portal experiences are customer-service focused, while generic ITSM portals center internal employee service flows.
They are identical portals with different themes and no difference in data model or workflow intent.
CSM portal is for agents and ITSM portal is for external contacts in partner support programs.
ITSM portal supports entitlements natively, while CSM portal requires custom plugins for account context.
csm.explanation: The CSM portal is customer-facing with brand customization, account-level data scoping (customers only see their own cases), and external user authentication. The ITSM portal serves internal employees with different navigation and features.

csm.q: What is the role of the customer_contact table vs the sys_user table in CSM?
options: customer_contact extends sys_user and adds CSM-specific fields like account, title, and partner — contacts are users with customer-specific attributes
They are completely separate tables with no relationship
customer_contact replaces sys_user for all CSM users
sys_user is for admins; customer_contact is for everyone else
csm.explanation: customer_contact extends sys_user, inheriting all user fields while adding CSM-specific fields (account, contact type, partner flag). This means contacts are full platform users with additional customer context.

csm.q: How does Case categorization work in CSM?
options: Cases use a multi-level categorization (Category → Subcategory → Type) that can drive automatic assignment, SLA selection, and knowledge article suggestions
Cases can only have one category level
Categorization is purely cosmetic and has no impact on processing
Categories are assigned randomly by the system
csm.explanation: Multi-level categorization drives automation: assignment rules match categories to teams, SLA definitions can target specific categories, and knowledge suggestions filter by category for relevant article recommendations.

csm.q: What is Customer Project Management in CSM?
options: A feature that allows customer-facing teams to manage projects, tasks, and milestones related to customer engagements such as implementations or onboarding
An internal project management tool unrelated to CSM
A method for customers to manage their own internal projects
A reporting module for project metrics
csm.explanation: Customer Project Management extends CSM with project capabilities for customer engagements. It tracks implementation projects, onboarding milestones, and deliverables with customer visibility through the portal.

csm.q: How does Agent Assist / AI Search help CSM agents?
options: It uses AI to analyze the case context and proactively recommend relevant Knowledge articles, similar cases, and next best actions to the agent in the workspace
It automatically resolves cases without agent involvement
It replaces the agent's typing with AI-generated responses
It only works for email-based cases
csm.explanation: Agent Assist (powered by Now Assist) analyzes case content in real-time and surfaces relevant KB articles, similar resolved cases, and recommended actions in the agent workspace sidebar, reducing resolution time.

csm.q: What is the purpose of the Installed Product table in CSM?
options: Tracks specific product instances installed or provisioned for a customer, including version, serial number, and warranty status — used to link cases to specific assets
Tracks ServiceNow platform installations
Records software installed on agent workstations
Stores product catalog items
csm.explanation: The Installed Product (sn_customerservice_installed_product) tracks what specific products a customer has, including versions and serial numbers. When a case is logged, agents can link it to the exact product instance experiencing the issue.

csm.q: What is the difference between a Case and a Case Task in CSM?
options: A Case tracks the overall customer issue; Case Tasks are sub-tasks assigned to different teams or individuals to complete parts of the case resolution — both extend the task table
Case Tasks are auto-created for every case
Cases and Case Tasks are on the same table
Case Tasks can exist without a parent Case
csm.explanation: Cases represent the customer's overall issue. Case Tasks break down the resolution work into assignable sub-tasks (e.g., 'Investigate logs', 'Test fix', 'Update customer'). Multiple tasks can run in parallel or sequence.

csm.q: How do you configure omnichannel routing in CSM?
options: Use Advanced Work Assignment (AWA) to define queues, matching rules, and agent capacity for routing cases from different channels (chat, phone, email) to qualified available agents
Create a separate queue per channel manually
Use Business Rules to assign cases randomly
Agents manually pick up cases from a shared list
csm.explanation: Advanced Work Assignment provides intelligent routing across all channels. It considers agent skills, capacity, availability, and affinity (routing returning customers to the same agent) to optimize case distribution.

csm.q: What is a Service Contract in CSM?
options: A record that defines the terms, duration, and scope of service provided to a customer — it drives entitlements and SLA targets for cases from that account
A legal document stored as an attachment
A type of catalog item
An internal service agreement between IT teams
csm.explanation: Service Contracts define what service a customer has purchased, including duration, coverage hours, and service levels. Entitlements are derived from contracts to automatically apply the correct SLA when a case is created.

csm.q: What is the CSM Community feature?
options: An online forum where customers can ask questions, share solutions, and interact with other customers and support staff — reducing case volume through peer support
An internal messaging system for agents
A social media integration
A team collaboration tool for CSM admins
csm.explanation: CSM Community provides a customer-facing forum for peer-to-peer support. Customers can post questions, share solutions, and vote on answers. Common questions get resolved without creating cases, deflecting support volume.

csm.q: How does the Customer Central workspace differ from the standard CSM agent workspace?
options: Customer Central unifies account-level context and outcomes, while agent workspace optimizes case execution workflows.
They are the same interface with different branding applied by role and theme configuration.
Customer Central is deprecated and should be replaced entirely by legacy CSM workspace modules.
Agent workspace is for external customers; Customer Central is for internal case assignment groups.
csm.explanation: Customer Central is an account-centric workspace giving agents a complete view of the customer relationship — all open cases, contract status, entitlements, installed products, and communication history — enabling more informed, contextual support.

csm.q: A CSM customer wants to implement proactive customer service that automatically creates cases when monitoring detects an issue affecting their service BEFORE the customer reports it. What is the architecture?
options: Use proactive service signals and account context to trigger cases/plays before customer-reported impact.
Open incidents for all telemetry anomalies and let account teams convert them to cases manually.
Create one weekly batch case per customer with all alerts to reduce case volume overhead.
Limit proactive service to VIP contacts because entitlement verification slows event-based automation.
csm.explanation: Proactive CSM architecture: Event Management detects infrastructure issues → Service Mapping identifies affected business services and linked customers → Automated case creation with customer-specific impact details → Proactive notifications via portal, email, and SMS before the customer is impacted.

csm.q: A customer with 500+ accounts wants customer-specific SLA targets. Some accounts have 1-hour response, others 4-hour, others 24-hour. How do you configure this without creating hundreds of SLA definitions?
options: Model account-aware SLA/entitlement rules with precedence strategy and transparent exception handling.
Duplicate case tables by SLA tier and route accounts to tables that match contracted response windows.
Keep one global SLA and apply account targets through client scripts at case form submit.
Store SLA logic in knowledge articles so agents can manually select the correct response target.
csm.explanation: The Entitlement model scales: one SLA Definition can reference entitlement targets. Each account's contract creates an entitlement with the specific duration. When a case is created, the system matches the account's entitlement to determine the correct SLA target dynamically.

csm.q: A global enterprise customer needs CSM configured for 3 regions (Americas, EMEA, APAC) with different business hours, languages, and routing rules. How do you architect this on a single instance?
options: Combine domain strategy, assignment/routing policy, and account hierarchy controls for regional operating models.
Deploy one CSM instance per region and synchronize accounts nightly to keep global reporting centralized.
Use catalog variables to encode region and let agents manually enforce local process variations.
Apply one global process and handle all regional exceptions through ad-hoc case comments and tasks.
csm.explanation: Single instance, regional configuration: Business Schedules define hours per region. SLAs reference region-specific schedules. AWA routes cases based on customer location to regional teams. Portal supports multiple languages. This avoids instance sprawl while respecting regional differences.

csm.q: You need to implement a tiered support model in CSM: Tier 1 handles first contact, Tier 2 handles technical investigation, Tier 3 is engineering. Each tier has different SLA targets. How do you track SLA per tier?
options: Implement tiered routing and escalation logic with ownership transitions and measurable handoff SLAs.
Assign all new cases to Tier 2, then downgrade simple issues to Tier 1 for closure speed.
Use one assignment group and model tiers only as case tags for simplified reporting.
Escalate all unresolved cases at fixed intervals regardless of severity or entitlement terms.
csm.explanation: Task-based tiered SLAs: the parent case has an overall resolution SLA. Each tier transition creates a case task with tier-specific SLA targets. This tracks per-tier performance (Tier 1 first response, Tier 2 investigation time, Tier 3 fix time) independently.

csm.q: A customer wants to measure Customer Effort Score (CES), CSAT, and NPS through their CSM portal. How do you implement this?
options: Use survey orchestration and metric governance so CES, CSAT, and NPS each serve distinct decision loops.
Capture only CSAT because CES and NPS overlap and add unnecessary survey fatigue.
Compute CES/NPS from case close duration and reopen rates instead of explicit customer responses.
Run one annual satisfaction survey and map all outputs to case-level feedback records.
csm.explanation: ServiceNow's Survey framework supports multiple survey types. Configure triggers (case closure, portal interaction) to send surveys. Link responses back to cases and accounts for correlation. PA dashboards show trends, and agents see customer sentiment in the workspace.

csm.q: A B2B customer needs partner companies to also handle cases on behalf of their mutual customers. Partners should see only their assigned cases and the shared customer's account data. How do you configure this?
options: Model account-contact-partner relationships with delegated access controls and clear case ownership boundaries.
Allow all partner users full account visibility to avoid delays in collaborative case handling.
Create separate accounts for each partner to prevent cross-company entitlement rule conflicts.
Use watch lists only; delegated partner access is unnecessary when email updates are enabled.
csm.explanation: CSM's Partner model supports multi-party service: Partner accounts and contacts with specific roles, ACLs scoping visibility to assigned cases and relevant account data, and partner portal access for case management — all without exposing unrelated customer data.

csm.q: A customer wants to implement self-service deflection that reduces case volume by 30%. What is the strategy using CSM capabilities?
options: Implement deflection via contextual knowledge, intent routing, and measurable containment funnels.
Hide live support entry points to force portal-only interactions and reduce inbound case count.
Publish static FAQs and disable search personalization to avoid exposing irrelevant articles.
Increase mandatory fields on case forms so customers self-solve before completing submission.
csm.explanation: Multi-layer deflection: Knowledge (AI-powered search surfaces relevant articles before case creation), Virtual Agent (handles routine queries conversationally), Community (peer answers for common questions), Service Catalog (structured requests that don't need cases). PA tracks deflection at each layer.

csm.q: A customer experiences a major outage affecting 200 accounts. 500 cases flood in within 30 minutes. How do you handle this with Major Issue Management?
options: Use major-incident style communication and parent-child case orchestration to contain surge volumes.
Merge all incoming cases into one record and close duplicates without customer notification.
Suspend SLA clocks on outage-related cases until root cause is confirmed by infrastructure teams.
Create ad-hoc task lists in spreadsheets and update case statuses in bulk at day end.
csm.explanation: Major Issue Management: create parent case with the outage details, configure matching rules (category + time window) to auto-link incoming cases, post portal status page updates, send proactive comms to affected accounts, and resolve the parent to cascade resolution/communication to all 500 child cases.

csm.q: What is the Proactive Case feature in CSM?
options: A capability that automatically creates cases for customers before they report an issue, based on monitoring data or known issues affecting their products/services
A case created by the customer proactively
A case escalation mechanism
A case template for common issues
csm.explanation: Proactive Cases are created automatically when the system detects an issue that will impact a customer (via Event Management, monitoring integration, or manual trigger). The customer is notified before they even experience the problem.

csm.q: How does the 'Related Cases' feature help agents in CSM?
options: It shows cases from the same account, with similar categories, or affecting the same product — helping agents identify patterns and link related issues
It only shows cases assigned to the same agent
It displays cases from all customers
It shows cases created on the same date
csm.explanation: Related Cases surfaces contextually relevant cases based on account, category, product, and other criteria. This helps agents identify recurring issues, link related problems, and leverage previous resolutions.

csm.q: What is a Service-Aware Case in CSM?
options: A case linked to a specific business service and its underlying infrastructure via CMDB relationships, enabling impact analysis and targeted troubleshooting
A case with SLA tracking enabled
A case created from the Service Catalog
A case assigned to a service team
csm.explanation: Service-Aware Cases connect the customer issue to the affected business service and its CMDB infrastructure. Agents can see the service topology, identify the impacted CI, and understand upstream/downstream effects.

csm.q: What is the purpose of the CSM Targeted Communication feature?
options: Targeted communication segments audiences by context and triggers relevant outreach at controlled lifecycle points.
It sends every service bulletin to all contacts so communication parity is preserved across accounts.
It replaces case comments by pushing one-way updates without relationship to case or account context.
It is limited to outbound email campaigns and cannot be tied to service events or incidents.
csm.explanation: Targeted Communications allow support teams to send segmented messages to groups of customers (e.g., all customers on Product X, all accounts in APAC). This is used for proactive notifications about maintenance, known issues, or service changes.

csm.q: A customer wants CSM integrated with their Salesforce CRM so that when a Salesforce opportunity becomes a customer, an Account is auto-created in ServiceNow CSM with all contact data synced bidirectionally. What is the architecture?
options: Integrate lifecycle signals bi-directionally with governed field mappings and ownership across CRM/CSM boundaries.
Use one-way sync from CSM to CRM only, since opportunity context should not influence support workflows.
Store Salesforce IDs in free-text fields and rely on agents to cross-reference account context manually.
Replicate CRM account/contact tables in CSM and disable sync to avoid reconciliation conflicts.
csm.explanation: Integration Hub Salesforce spoke provides pre-built actions for CRUD operations. Bidirectional sync requires: initial migration via transform maps, ongoing scheduled flows for new/updated records, field mapping between CRM and CSM data models, and conflict resolution (last-write-wins or field-level rules).

csm.q: A customer needs to implement AI-powered case classification that automatically sets category, priority, and assignment group based on the case description. How do you architect this?
options: Use model governance, confidence thresholds, and fallback routing to keep AI classification reliable in production.
Auto-accept all model predictions to maximize throughput and retrain quarterly on unresolved cases only.
Train separate model per assignment group and ignore shared taxonomy to improve local precision.
Run AI only on closed cases so misclassification cannot affect live customer response paths.
csm.explanation: Predictive Intelligence trains ML models on historical labeled cases. The model analyzes new case descriptions and predicts category, priority, and other fields. Auto-classification reduces agent triage time. Agent override ensures human judgment prevails when the model is uncertain.

csm.q: What is the sn_customerservice_case table?
options: The primary table for CSM cases — it extends the task table and stores all customer service case records
The incident table used by CSM
A staging table for case imports
A reporting table for case metrics
csm.explanation: sn_customerservice_case is the core CSM case table. It extends task, inheriting task fields (state, priority, assignment) while adding CSM-specific fields (account, contact, product, entitlement).

csm.q: What is a Case Channel in CSM?
options: The method through which a case was created or received — such as phone, email, portal, chat, or social media
A TV channel about customer service
A communication template
A routing queue
csm.explanation: The Channel field on a case records how the customer contacted support. This data drives channel-specific SLA targets, routing rules, and analytics about customer channel preferences.

csm.q: What is an Account Team in CSM?
options: A designated group of people (account manager, technical lead, support lead) assigned to manage a specific customer account
All agents in the support department
The customer organization team
A team that creates new accounts
csm.explanation: Account Teams define the relationship between support staff and customer accounts. Roles like Account Manager, Technical Lead, and Support Lead can be assigned per account for relationship management.

csm.q: How does CSM handle case escalation?
options: Escalation combines SLA/priority conditions, ownership transitions, and communication obligations.
Escalation simply reassigns to manager group after fixed time regardless of entitlement or severity.
Escalation closes the original case and opens a new one at a higher support tier automatically.
Escalation is triggered only by customer sentiment score and not by operational SLA breach conditions.
csm.explanation: CSM escalation uses SLA-driven rules (auto-escalate before breach), inactivity monitors (escalate stale cases), and manual escalation actions. Escalation can change assignment, priority, and trigger notifications to management.

csm.q: What is the relationship between Entitlements and SLAs in CSM?
options: Entitlements determine service rights and SLA selection logic, binding contractual support rules to case handling.
Entitlements are optional labels for reporting, while SLA definitions apply uniformly to all accounts.
Entitlements replace SLAs by directly controlling pause/resume timers through contact preference settings.
Entitlements are evaluated only at case closure when final response time is calculated for reporting.
csm.explanation: Entitlements specify per-customer (or per-product, per-contract) service commitments. SLA Definitions reference entitlement data to dynamically set targets. This allows one SLA definition to serve multiple customer tiers.

csm.q: What is the CSM Case Form Agent Assist panel?
options: A sidebar panel in the agent workspace that proactively suggests relevant Knowledge articles, similar cases, and recommended actions based on the current case context
A form for agents to request assistance from managers
A training module within the workspace
A customer-facing help panel
csm.explanation: The Agent Assist panel uses contextual analysis to surface helpful information: KB articles matching the case description, previously resolved similar cases, and AI-recommended next actions — all without the agent needing to search manually.

csm.q: How does the Asset and Entitlement Verification work when a case is created?
options: Asset/entitlement checks validate support eligibility and route case treatment based on covered products/services.
Verification is informational only; assignment and SLA logic should ignore entitlement state for speed.
Asset checks run after closure to enrich reporting and do not affect active case workflow paths.
Entitlement verification requires manual override each time because account relationships are too dynamic.
csm.explanation: Automatic entitlement verification checks: Is there an active contract for this account? Does it cover this product? Is the support window active? If verification fails, agents see a warning and can still create the case but with appropriate documentation.

csm.q: What is the purpose of the Communication Plan in CSM?
options: Communication plans define timing/channels/audiences so updates remain consistent during service-impact events.
They are templates for agent signatures and have no relationship to case lifecycle communications.
They replace notifications and require manual send by supervisors for every status transition.
They are used only for marketing outreach and should not be tied to support operations.
csm.explanation: Communication Plans automate customer updates during case lifecycle. Configure triggers (e.g., every 24 hours while case is open, on state change, on approaching SLA breach) to send templated updates, reducing customer follow-up calls.

csm.q: What is the CSM Interaction record?
options: Interaction captures omnichannel engagement context and can be converted/linked to downstream work records.
Interaction is a billing object used to aggregate chargeback totals per support session.
Interaction replaces cases entirely in CSM and should be used for all lifecycle management tasks.
Interaction is a read-only audit table populated only by email inbound processing rules.
csm.explanation: Interaction records log every customer touchpoint with metadata (channel, duration, agent, disposition). They build a complete communication timeline visible to agents, enabling context-aware support across channels.

csm.q: A customer wants to implement a customer health scoring system that predicts churn risk based on case history, SLA performance, survey scores, and product usage. How do you architect this in CSM?
options: Build composite health scoring with weighted indicators, drift monitoring, and action playbooks tied to thresholds.
Use one static health formula for all accounts so trend comparisons remain globally consistent.
Score accounts only by open case count because support load is the strongest churn predictor.
Recalculate health quarterly and let account teams decide interventions without automated triggers.
csm.explanation: Customer Health Score architecture: PA indicators aggregate signals (case trends, SLA breaches, survey sentiment, engagement metrics). Predictive Intelligence models identify churn patterns from historical data. Automated alerts trigger when scores decline, enabling proactive account management.

csm.q: A customer needs to support 10,000 B2B contacts and 500,000 B2C consumers on the same CSM instance. How do you handle the vastly different scale, authentication, and portal requirements?
options: Separate B2B and B2C experiences through controlled segmentation while preserving shared service capabilities.
Use one universal portal journey and ask users to self-identify as consumer or business on each case.
Create dedicated CSM instance for B2C and sync only severe cases back to B2B operations.
Store consumers as contacts under one generic account to simplify entitlement and data model complexity.
csm.explanation: Dual-model CSM: B2B portal with SAML SSO, account-scoped views, and dedicated account teams. B2C portal with consumer-friendly auth (social, email), self-service focus, and Virtual Agent for scale. Shared backend with segment-specific routing, SLAs, and entitlements.

csm.q: An airline wants to use CSM where a single flight delay event creates cases for 300 affected passengers, each needing rebooking and compensation calculations. How do you handle this volume efficiently?
options: Use event-to-case orchestration with parent-case communication strategy and passenger-specific context linking.
Create one bulk case for all passengers and broadcast updates through outbound email campaigns only.
Open incident records instead of CSM cases so flight operations can process impact at infrastructure level.
Queue all passenger cases for manual triage before any communication to prevent inaccurate outage messaging.
csm.explanation: Mass event handling: Major Issue parent case tracks the flight delay. Flow Designer generates child cases from passenger manifest data. Playbooks guide agents through rebooking/compensation steps per passenger. Targeted Communications send bulk updates. Child case resolution cascades from parent when the issue is resolved.

csm.q: What is the role of the Customer Service Management (CSM) data model hierarchy?
options: The CSM data model follows a hierarchy: Account → Contact → Case → Case Task, with Products and Entitlements linking to Accounts, and Service Contracts defining the service terms
All CSM records are stored in a single flat table
The hierarchy is Account → Case only
Cases are not related to any account or contact
csm.explanation: The CSM data model is hierarchical: Accounts (customers) have Contacts (people), who create Cases (issues). Cases spawn Case Tasks (sub-work). Products, Entitlements, and Contracts link to Accounts to define what support is available.

csm.q: What is the difference between Quick Close and Full Resolution of a case?
options: Quick Close applies streamlined closure for simple resolution paths; Full Resolution captures complete closure details/workflow.
Quick Close bypasses entitlement/SLA checks, while Full Resolution enforces them after closure.
They are equivalent actions with different labels for partner-facing and customer-facing portals.
Full Resolution should be used only for escalated cases; Quick Close is mandatory for standard incidents.
csm.explanation: Quick Close is a streamlined action for simple, first-contact resolutions (e.g., answered a question). It sets resolution fields and closes in one click. Full Resolution follows the standard lifecycle with investigation, root cause, and detailed resolution notes.

csm.q: What is the "Watched Cases" feature in the CSM portal?
options: Allows contacts to follow cases they did not create — receiving updates when the case state changes, useful for managers monitoring their team cases
A security audit feature that tracks who viewed a case
A dashboard that shows trending case categories
An admin tool for monitoring agent performance
csm.explanation: Watched Cases let portal users subscribe to cases opened by other contacts at their account. They receive notifications on updates, enabling managers or project leads to stay informed without being the case opener.

csm.q: What is the difference between a Service Entitlement and a Product Entitlement?
options: Service entitlement usually governs contracted service scope/levels, while product entitlement validates support rights for specific covered products.
Service entitlement is used only for billing display, while product entitlement is the sole source of SLA calculation.
Product entitlement replaces account entitlement; service entitlement is deprecated in modern CSM deployments.
Both entitlement types are synonyms and are interchangeable without impact on case routing or SLA behavior.
csm.explanation: Service Entitlements are tied to service contracts and define general support terms (hours, channels, response times). Product Entitlements are specific to products and may have different support terms based on warranty, subscription, or product tier.

csm.q: What happens when a customer submits a case through the CSM portal?
options: A case record is created on the sn_customerservice_case table, the customer receives a confirmation, and the case enters the assignment/routing workflow
An email is sent to a shared inbox for manual processing
A task is created on the task table with no assignment
Nothing happens until an agent reviews the submission
csm.explanation: Portal case submission creates a case record, triggers automated routing (Assignment Rules or AWA), sends confirmation to the customer, and optionally triggers SLA attachment and entitlement verification.

csm.q: How does Skill-Based Routing work in CSM?
options: Skill-based routing aligns case demand with agent capability profiles using configurable matching and queue policy.
It routes strictly by assignment group hierarchy and ignores individual capability metadata.
It is a reporting feature only; assignment still depends exclusively on manual triage.
It requires one unique case table per skill domain to avoid cross-skill assignment conflicts.
csm.explanation: Skill-Based Routing in AWA matches case requirements (product, language, complexity) against agent skill profiles. The system considers skill proficiency, capacity, and availability to route to the best-qualified agent.

csm.q: A telecom company needs CSM to handle 50,000 cases per month across 3 support tiers, 5 product lines, and 4 languages. How do you design the assignment and routing architecture?
options: Design scalable routing, tier governance, and product-region skills with workload balancing and queue controls.
Assign by round-robin globally and let supervisors re-route cases manually to specialist groups.
Create one queue per product-region-tier combination and disable overflow to preserve ownership clarity.
Route all premium customers to Tier 3 directly to reduce reassignments and total touch time.
csm.explanation: High-volume routing: AWA handles multi-criteria matching (product skill + language + tier). Capacity management prevents overload. Tier queues with auto-escalation SLAs move cases up. Agent affinity improves customer experience by routing returning customers to familiar agents.

csm.q: What is the purpose of the Customer Service Management (CSM) Dashboard?
options: CSM dashboards aggregate operational KPIs for oversight, trend monitoring, and resource/experience decisions.
Dashboards replace all reports and should be the single source for audit-grade evidence exports.
Dashboards are intended for agents only and should not be used by managers or operations leads.
Dashboards calculate SLA timers directly, making separate SLA engine configuration unnecessary.
csm.explanation: CSM Dashboards aggregate operational KPIs: case backlog, SLA performance, first contact resolution rate, CSAT, and agent metrics. Managers use them for real-time oversight and capacity planning.

csm.q: What is Case State in CSM?
options: The current lifecycle stage of a case (e.g., New, In Progress, Awaiting Customer, Resolved, Closed) that drives workflow, SLA, and communication behavior
The geographic location where the case was created
The severity rating of the case
The customer account state
csm.explanation: Case State tracks lifecycle progression. State transitions can be configured to trigger actions (notifications, SLA events, task creation). Common states: New → In Progress → Awaiting Info → Resolved → Closed.

csm.q: What is the First Contact Resolution (FCR) metric in CSM?
options: FCR measures cases resolved in the initial contact cycle without follow-up rework or escalation.
FCR counts any case closed within one business day regardless of transfer or reopen behavior.
FCR is equivalent to CSAT when surveys are sent immediately after closure.
FCR is computed only for phone channel interactions and excluded from digital support channels.
csm.explanation: FCR measures how often cases are resolved in the initial interaction. High FCR indicates effective agents, good knowledge tools, and proper training. It correlates strongly with customer satisfaction and operational efficiency.

csm.q: A customer wants to implement a Knowledge-Centered Service (KCS) methodology within CSM where agents create and improve Knowledge articles as part of case resolution. How do you configure this?
options: Operationalize KCS with article lifecycle governance, solve-loop behavior, and measurable reuse quality metrics.
Require agents to publish an article for every case before closure regardless of content maturity.
Separate knowledge authoring from support teams so case handling speed is not impacted by documentation.
Archive low-view articles monthly and republish only after customer request confirms missing content.
csm.explanation: KCS in CSM: agents create/flag articles during case resolution ("solve and evolve"). Article templates pre-populate from case data. Peer review workflows ensure quality. Analytics track which articles deflect future cases. Agent contribution metrics incentivize participation.

csm.q: What is the purpose of the Disposition field on a CSM interaction record?
options: Records the outcome of the interaction — such as "Resolved", "Transferred", "Follow-up Required", "Escalated" — enabling reporting on interaction effectiveness
Sets the emotional tone of the interaction
Determines which agent handles the next interaction
Controls the display format of the interaction
csm.explanation: Disposition captures what happened during an interaction. It enables reporting on first-call resolution, transfer rates, and escalation frequency. Different dispositions can trigger different follow-up actions.

grc.q: What does GRC stand for in ServiceNow?
options: Governance, Risk, and Compliance
General Record Configuration
Global Resource Center
Group Role Control
grc.explanation: GRC stands for Governance, Risk, and Compliance — a suite of applications for managing organizational risks, policies, and regulatory compliance.

grc.q: What is a Policy in ServiceNow GRC?
options: A policy defines formal governance expectations and required behavior for people, process, and technology.
A policy is a one-time checklist used only during initial compliance implementation projects.
A policy is a real-time monitoring script that automatically closes non-compliant records.
A policy is equivalent to a control test result and should not be maintained separately.
grc.explanation: GRC Policies are formal organizational rules tracked in ServiceNow. They include lifecycle management, acknowledgment tracking, and compliance verification.

grc.q: What is a Risk in ServiceNow GRC?
options: A risk is potential uncertainty that could affect objectives if it materializes.
A risk is any issue that has already happened and been permanently resolved.
A risk is a control deficiency that has no business impact scoring requirements.
A risk is a vendor questionnaire response awaiting procurement approval and onboarding.
grc.explanation: Risks in GRC are potential threats assessed by likelihood (probability) and impact (severity). They are linked to business processes, controls, and entities for structured risk management.

grc.q: What is a Control in GRC?
options: A control is a preventive/detective mechanism used to reduce risk and demonstrate compliance intent.
A control is any audit comment captured during yearly assessment workshops with process owners.
A control is the same as a policy acknowledgment by an employee in portal onboarding tasks.
A control is a remediation ticket used only after incidents have already caused business impact.
grc.explanation: Controls are the safeguards organizations implement to manage risks and meet compliance requirements. They can be preventive (stop issues), detective (find issues), or corrective (fix issues).

grc.q: What is a Control Test in GRC?
options: A control test evaluates whether a control is designed/operating effectively over a defined period.
A control test is a policy publication event that records user acknowledgment timestamps.
A control test is a workflow notification sent to auditors after risk acceptance approval.
A control test is the same as incident postmortem review for any sev-1 outage event.
grc.explanation: Control Tests validate that controls are functioning as designed. Testers collect evidence (screenshots, reports, data), record findings, and mark the control as effective or deficient.

grc.q: What is the Unified Compliance Framework (UCF) in ServiceNow GRC?
options: UCF normalizes regulatory requirements into a reusable control model to reduce duplicate compliance effort.
UCF is a reporting plugin that exports audit PDFs and does not influence control design or mapping.
UCF replaces policy lifecycle management by storing all obligations directly on risk statements.
UCF is intended only for finance frameworks and cannot map technical/security compliance obligations.
grc.explanation: UCF provides a pre-built library of common controls mapped across multiple regulatory frameworks. This allows organizations to implement one control that satisfies requirements from multiple regulations simultaneously.

grc.q: How does Risk Scoring work in ServiceNow GRC?
options: Risk scoring combines defined factors/weights and governance rules to produce comparable, explainable risk ratings.
Risk scores should be manually assigned by auditors to avoid model bias from automated calculations.
Risk scoring is derived exclusively from control pass/fail rates and ignores business impact dimensions.
Risk scores are recalculated only at quarter close to maintain stable executive reporting baselines.
grc.explanation: The risk scoring matrix multiplies Likelihood (1-5) by Impact (1-5) to produce a risk score. Thresholds determine risk ratings. Inherent risk (before controls) and residual risk (after controls) are tracked separately.

grc.q: What is the difference between an Issue and a Risk in GRC?
options: A risk represents uncertain future exposure; an issue reflects a realized problem requiring active remediation.
Issue and risk are equivalent terms in GRC and differ only by which dashboard displays the record.
Issues are always strategic and long-term, while risks are always immediate operational incidents.
A risk is created only after failure occurs; issues are used to predict potential future events.
grc.explanation: Risks represent potential threats (forward-looking). Issues represent actual findings or problems (current state) — often discovered through control testing, audits, or incident analysis. Issues require remediation plans with deadlines.

grc.q: What is Policy and Compliance Management in GRC?
options: Policy and Compliance Management maps obligations to policies/controls and tracks adherence evidence over time.
Policy Management is only document storage; compliance evidence must remain external to avoid audit lock-in.
Compliance Management replaces control testing because policy acknowledgments are considered sufficient proof.
Policy and Compliance is limited to annual audits and should not be integrated with operational workflows.
grc.explanation: Policy and Compliance Management handles policy lifecycle: draft → review → approve → publish → distribute. It tracks who has acknowledged policies, monitors compliance exceptions, and manages policy retirement.

grc.q: What is Vendor Risk Management in ServiceNow GRC?
options: Vendor risk management governs third-party assessments, controls, and remediation through lifecycle oversight.
It is primarily a procurement function and should remain outside GRC to avoid duplicate workflows.
Vendor risk should be tracked as incidents because third-party issues are operational by definition.
Once onboarding is complete, vendor risk posture is assumed stable unless contract terms change.
grc.explanation: Vendor Risk Management assesses third-party risks through tiering (critical, high, medium, low vendors), risk questionnaires, due diligence evidence collection, and continuous monitoring of vendor risk posture.

grc.q: How does the Risk Heat Map work in GRC?
options: Heat maps visualize likelihood/impact distributions to prioritize treatment and communicate risk concentration.
Heat maps replace risk scoring by converting all risks into high/medium/low categories only.
Heat maps are compliance artifacts and should not influence operational remediation sequencing.
Heat maps should include only accepted risks so leadership sees final residual exposure posture.
grc.explanation: The Risk Heat Map is a 2D matrix visualization. Risks are plotted by their likelihood and impact scores. Colors (red/amber/yellow/green) indicate severity zones. This enables executives to quickly identify where the organization's greatest risks lie.

grc.q: What is an Authority Document in GRC?
options: A regulatory framework, standard, or law (e.g., SOX, HIPAA, ISO 27001) that the organization must comply with — it contains citations that map to controls
An internal knowledge base article
A user manual for the GRC application
A system administrator's documentation
grc.explanation: Authority Documents represent external regulations and standards (SOX, HIPAA, GDPR, ISO 27001, etc.). Citations within these documents map to specific control requirements, establishing the compliance framework.

grc.q: A financial services company needs to implement continuous control monitoring with automated evidence collection across 5 regulatory frameworks. How would you architect this in ServiceNow GRC?
options: Implement automated evidence collection and control testing with exception workflows and audit-ready traceability.
Run annual spreadsheet attestations only, then import final scores into GRC before audit season.
Create one universal control template and apply identical frequency/testing to all control families.
Track findings in incident records and map them to controls manually after each audit cycle.
grc.explanation: Continuous monitoring architecture: UCF harmonizes controls across frameworks (one control, multiple regulations). Integration Hub automates evidence collection. Scheduled test execution provides continuous assessment. Automated scoring highlights gaps. Performance Analytics dashboards give regulatory-specific views.

grc.q: An organization is preparing for a SOX audit and needs to demonstrate control effectiveness across 200+ controls. The audit is in 8 weeks. How do you prepare using ServiceNow GRC?
options: Model control objectives, evidence, and test cadence in platform with clear ownership and attestation history.
Store auditor notes in knowledge articles and attach screenshots only when external auditors request them.
Use policy exceptions as control evidence because approval history is sufficient for effectiveness claims.
Close failed tests quickly and reopen only if audit asks for prior-period control execution proof.
grc.explanation: Audit prep: gap assessment identifies untested controls, risk-based prioritization focuses on what matters most, automated testing accelerates evidence collection, issue remediation addresses gaps before the auditor arrives, and audit-ready reports provide the complete evidence package.

grc.q: An organization needs to implement a Third-Party Risk Management program that assesses 500+ vendors annually. Manual questionnaire processing takes 6 months. How do you automate this?
options: Use scalable intake, tiered assessment, and continuous monitoring signals with remediation governance.
Assess only top-tier vendors annually and waive remaining vendors through risk acceptance templates.
Treat questionnaire completion as equivalent to control validation to accelerate onboarding throughput.
Move all vendor assessments to procurement workflow and import final ratings to GRC quarterly.
grc.explanation: Automated VRM: tier vendors by criticality (Tier 1 gets deep assessment, Tier 3 gets basic). Digital questionnaires with auto-scoring eliminate manual review. External risk feeds (security ratings, news monitoring) provide continuous assessment between formal reviews. Automated schedules ensure nothing falls through cracks.

grc.q: What is a Risk Framework in ServiceNow GRC?
options: A risk framework defines taxonomy, scoring, and governance structure for consistent risk management execution.
A risk framework is a one-time audit template used only during annual compliance assessments.
A risk framework replaces policy management because controls are inherited directly from risk records.
A risk framework is optional when incidents and problems are already tracked in ITSM modules.
grc.explanation: Risk Frameworks define the organizational approach to risk management: how risks are categorized (operational, financial, compliance), how they are scored (qualitative, quantitative), risk appetite definitions, and escalation rules.

grc.q: What is a Risk Appetite statement in GRC?
options: Risk appetite defines acceptable risk boundaries to guide decision-making, treatment choices, and escalation thresholds.
Risk appetite is the list of all risks currently accepted with no requirement for threshold articulation.
Risk appetite is a technical control matrix generated from vulnerability scanners each quarter.
Risk appetite is a financial reserve model used only for cyber-insurance premium calculations.
grc.explanation: Risk Appetite defines acceptable risk levels. If a risk score exceeds the appetite threshold, it requires escalation and mitigation. Different business areas may have different risk appetites (e.g., lower for compliance, higher for innovation).

grc.q: How does GRC integrate with ITSM in ServiceNow?
options: GRC-ITSM integration links risk/control obligations to operational work for traceable remediation execution.
Integration should be avoided because ITSM ticket lifecycle introduces unnecessary compliance complexity.
GRC should consume only closed incident data to prevent premature compliance reporting fluctuations.
Integration is limited to change management and cannot support control deficiency remediation workflows.
grc.explanation: GRC-ITSM integration: control failures create incidents for remediation, risk events trigger change requests, incident trends feed risk indicators, and CMDB data enriches risk assessments. This closed-loop approach connects compliance with operations.

grc.q: What is a Risk Register?
options: A risk register is a structured inventory of identified risks, scores, ownership, and treatment status.
A risk register is a static archive of closed issues with no requirement for active ownership.
A risk register is a policy library used only to classify authority documents by framework.
A risk register is a list of all exceptions automatically accepted by system administrators.
grc.explanation: The Risk Register is the central repository of all identified risks. It tracks each risk description, assessment (likelihood × impact), owner, mitigation plan, status, and review dates.

grc.q: What does "residual risk" mean in GRC?
options: Residual risk is the remaining exposure after controls and treatments are applied.
Residual risk is the initial inherent score before any controls are selected or tested.
Residual risk is the average score of all risks in a domain regardless of treatment state.
Residual risk is the amount of risk transferred to vendors through contract obligations.
grc.explanation: Residual risk = Inherent risk - Control effectiveness. After applying all controls and mitigations, the remaining risk exposure is the residual risk. If residual risk exceeds risk appetite, additional controls are needed.

grc.q: A multinational company needs to comply with GDPR, SOX, HIPAA, and ISO 27001 simultaneously. Many controls overlap across frameworks. How do you minimize duplicated effort while maintaining framework-specific evidence?
options: Design a unified control framework with mapped obligations, reusable controls, and jurisdiction-aware evidence handling.
Maintain separate compliance apps per regulation to avoid cross-framework control mapping complexity.
Adopt strictest regulation globally and ignore local variance to simplify policy administration.
Use one quarterly self-attestation form for all standards and treat non-response as implicit compliance.
grc.explanation: Control harmonization through UCF: identify where frameworks share requirements (e.g., access control appears in all four). Implement once, test once, but tag evidence with framework-specific metadata. Reporting filters by framework to produce auditor-ready packages per regulation.

cis_df.q: A CMDB administrator needs to verify that stale or no-longer-useful data is removed from the CMDB. Which governance capability supports this?
options: CI Class Manager
CMDB and CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard
CMDB Data Manager
De-duplication Templates
cis_df.explanation: CMDB Data Manager provides governance policies (attestation, archive, delete, retire) that help remove stale or irrelevant CMDB data.

cis_df.q: Which policy types can be created within CMDB Data Manager? (Choose 2)
options: De-duplication
Archive
Reconciliation
Retire
cis_df.explanation: CMDB Data Manager includes policy types such as de-duplication, archive, delete, and retire. Reconciliation is handled by IRE/reconciliation rules, not Data Manager policy type selection.

cis_df.q: From CMDB Workspace, which actions can be initiated directly? (Choose 2)
options: Execute ServiceNow Discovery
Create a CMDB Data Manager certification policy
Remediate duplicate CI records
Create a new CMDB class
cis_df.explanation: CMDB Workspace supports operational actions like triggering discovery workflows and duplicate remediation flows.

cis_df.q: A CMDB administrator changes the query for the SCCM Service Graph Connector. What is the likely impact?
options: The data source is automatically deactivated
Related scheduled jobs need to be reviewed/configured
All connector updates are skipped during upgrades
Connector mappings are permanently deleted
cis_df.explanation: Changing connector query behavior usually requires verifying associated schedules/jobs so ingestion runs as expected.

cis_df.q: Using baseline Data Manager policies, what condition must a CI meet before it can be archived or deleted?
options: Be marked as active
Be marked as critical
Be retired and end-of-life
Be fully operational and in use
cis_df.explanation: Archive/delete should only apply to CIs that are already retired/end-of-life according to governance policy.

cis_df.q: In the CSDM Data Foundations Dashboard, which tab provides alignment metrics for product models, locations, and business units?
options: Run
Foundation
Crawl
Walk
cis_df.explanation: The Foundation view focuses on baseline data-quality alignment metrics tied to CSDM fundamentals.

cis_df.q: To remove short-lived CIs that have not been discovered recently, what action is recommended after retiring them?
options: Create a delete policy
Create a scheduled job
Create a business rule
Run an import set
cis_df.explanation: Retire first, then use a governed delete policy to remove old CIs in a controlled manner.

cis_df.q: A team wants to document class attributes, identification/reconciliation behavior, and suggested relationships. Which capability best supports this?
options: CMDB Data Manager
CI Class Manager
CMDB Workspace
CMDB Health Preferences
cis_df.explanation: CI Class Manager is designed for class-level metadata, governance settings, and relationship modeling.

cis_df.q: Where can CMDB 360 / Multisource saved queries be viewed and created in CMDB Workspace?
options: CMDB Query Builder only
Coverage panel on CMDB 360 tab
Saved Queries panel on CMDB 360 tab
Saved Queries panel on Insights tab
cis_df.explanation: CMDB 360 includes a dedicated saved-query experience for reusable multisource views.

cis_df.q: How do you restrict which classes appear in a CI reference field on records such as Incident?
options: Set Principal Class from CI Class Manager basic class settings
Set Principal Class from CMDB Workspace home tab
Set Principal Class directly on each CI record
Set Principal Class in Discovery schedules
cis_df.explanation: Principal Class configuration in CI Class Manager controls which classes are prioritized/available in many CI selection contexts.

cis_df.q: Compared to classic service maps, what are additional Unified Map capabilities? (Choose 2)
options: Display depth can be adjusted
Nodes can be filtered by user preferences
Zoom controls are unavailable
Only one map level is supported
cis_df.explanation: Unified Map supports interactive depth/level tuning and user-driven filtering for faster analysis.

cis_df.q: When configuring Data Manager task assignment by user-group fields, which default groups are commonly available? (Choose 2)
options: Managed By Group
Support Group
Assignment Group
Approval Group
cis_df.explanation: In many CMDB governance setups, Managed By Group and Support Group are standard ownership-oriented fields for task routing.

cis_df.q: After enabling CSDM lifecycle sync, what is the next best action?
options: Activate lifecycle field mappings
Disable discrepancy report
Delete legacy lifecycle data
Run discovery reclassification first
cis_df.explanation: Lifecycle sync setup is followed by activating and validating lifecycle mappings so status propagation works as intended.

cis_df.q: Which characteristics/functions align with ServiceNow IntegrationHub ETL in CMDB programs? (Choose 2)
options: Integrates third-party data into CMDB/non-CMDB targets
Uses IRE for authoritative identification/reconciliation processing
Replaces Discovery for all use cases
Disables Service Graph Connectors
cis_df.explanation: IntegrationHub ETL brings external data in and can route through IRE-compatible governance, while Discovery and Service Graph remain complementary options.

cis_df.q: For fastest time-to-value ingest of Microsoft SCCM data into CMDB, which method is typically preferred?
options: Import Sets with manual transforms
Agent Client Collector
Service Graph Connector
